subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept long-term ownership of the custom asynchronous glob-parity implementation and cooperative `agent:bootstrap` hook scheduling, rather than retain the current Node runtime behavior?
rationale: The remaining question is not a narrow mechanical repair: it selects the permanent compatibility and maintenance boundary for configured bootstrap files and hook execution timing.

options.title: Accept the owned runtime contract
options.body: Have an agent-runtime owner confirm the intended glob and hook-scheduling semantics, then rebase and refresh current-head validation before merge.

options.title: Narrow the performance change
options.body: Retain the existing glob implementation and land only independently safe async read or diagnostic work if the project does not want to own custom glob parity.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Close or defer this branch if no owner wants to support the expanded filesystem-parity and scheduling surface.

recommendation.title: Accept the owned runtime contract
recommendation.body: Have an agent-runtime owner confirm the intended glob and hook-scheduling semantics, then rebase and refresh current-head validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows direct notification on this runtime-performance PR, while no stronger feature-history owner is established in the supplied context.
